findings.title: canManage() on V2 grants manage when the caller only has VIEW on groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). Because VIEW is in the accepted scope list, a caller whose only grant on the all-groups resource is VIEW passes canManage(). The no-argument requireManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /groups) calls, so a VIEW-only admin can create top-level groups. canView() correctly accepts VIEW and MANAGE; canManage() should accept MANAGE only. The GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() javadoc (lines 75-76) repeats the wrong 'VIEW or MANAGE' semantics. No test checks that a VIEW-only admin is denied group creation.

findings.title: Deleting any group fails when V2 admin permissions are enabled
findings.body: The GroupRemovedEvent listener calls management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) for every group removal. In V2 mode management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, which now returns GroupPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled (GroupPermissionsV2 lines 173-175) throws UnsupportedOperationException. The listener runs on every group deletion, whether or not the realm uses fine-grained admin permissions. Before this PR, V2 used the V1 GroupPermissions, where this call was a no-op for realms without permissions. With both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, group deletion will likely fail with an exception propagating out of event publishing. The test cleanup in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest (realm.cleanup().add(r -> r.groups().group(...).remove())) would hit the same path.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns internal resource UUIDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: Callers treat the returned set as group IDs: it is set as the UserModel.GROUPS session filter in UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource, and passed to getUsersCount. Here, granted.add(groupResource.getId()) adds the internal UUID of the authz Resource record, not the group ID. The resource name is the group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup). The V1 implementation correctly uses getName() with the prefix stripped. Line 122 has the same problem: hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) looks up the resource by name, so the UUID never matches, and the code silently falls back to the all-groups resource. The all-groups 'Groups' resource is itself returned by findByType and can add its own UUID to the set. Result: user search and count are filtered by IDs that match no group, so admins with per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS lose results, and the all-groups case adds garbage IDs.

findings.title: Group management-permissions endpoints now throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2 realms
findings.body: MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override groups() before this PR, so V2 realms used the V1 GroupPermissions for group management permissions. The PR replaces that with GroupPermissionsV2, where isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource and the *Permission accessors all throw UnsupportedOperationException. GroupResource.getManagementPermissions and setManagementPermissionsEnabled reach these, so the endpoints return HTTP 500 in V2 mode. This is a regression for groups, and the PR does not document it or gate the endpoints with a clear error.

findings.title: IMPERSONATE is evaluated against the target user's identity when a requester client is given
findings.body: When requester != null, the evaluation context is built with new UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user), i.e. the impersonated target user. The IMPERSONATE scope is an admin-side permission, and the requester==null path (line 70) evaluates with the admin's identity. The two paths therefore disagree. The target-identity context was copied from V1 isImpersonatable(), which uses it for the USER_IMPERSONATED scope, where it is correct. Here, user or role policies that should match the admin (or the requesting client via kc.client.id) are checked against the victim user, so canClientImpersonate/canImpersonate(user, client) can deny legitimate impersonation or match on the wrong identity.

findings.title: Existing FGAP v2 realms never get the Groups resource type; null is dereferenced
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists (line 250). Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this PR therefore never receive the Groups resource or the manage-members, view-members and manage-membership scopes. getResourceTypeResource(GROUPS) then returns null. Line 147 passes that null to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), which will likely NPE on every group check that falls back to the type-level resource. Creating a group permission in such a realm also fails in getOrCreateResource with 'No scopes found.'. This is an upgrade break unless a migration exists elsewhere, and none is in this diff.

findings.title: init() does not add the Groups type to realms that already have admin permissions
findings.body: The early return when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null means the new GROUPS resource type, its resource and its scopes are only created for newly enabled realms. This is the upgrade gap described in the GroupPermissionsV2 finding: existing realms have no 'Groups' resource and no group scopes, and nothing in the diff backfills them.

findings.title: Removed global canView short-circuit makes the list path evaluate policies per group
findings.body: The previous code computed canView() once and skipped per-group checks when it was true. Now filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) calls canView(group) for every group. In V2, canView(group) runs hasPermission, which resolves the per-group resource and evaluates the authorization policy engine each time, or falls back to the all-groups resource. For admins with global view, listing N groups costs N policy evaluations instead of one. GroupResource.getSubGroups has the same change.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. It should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel), which is the method it actually calls.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission javadoc says Stream but the method returns Set
findings.body: The @return tag says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method returns Set<String>. The javadoc also says it returns an empty set only when canView() is true, but the implementation also returns an empty set when the caller is not in the same realm or the server is missing.

findings.title: switch on resourceType throws NPE for null, where the old code was null-safe
findings.body: The previous code compared with USERS.getType().equals(resourceType), which is null-safe. The new switch (resourceType) throws NullPointerException when resourceType is null, instead of the intended error path. Callers must guarantee a non-null type or the failure becomes an NPE rather than a clear validation error.

findings.title: No test checks that a VIEW-only all-groups admin is denied group creation
findings.body: testViewGroups grants VIEW on all groups and only checks listing. The VIEW-only canManage() bug in GroupPermissionsV2 allows POST /groups for such an admin, and nothing in this test class catches it. A negative assertion (create top-level group with only all-groups VIEW gets FORBIDDEN) is needed. Similarly, nothing checks that group user-search or count results are correct when the admin has per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS, which the group-ID bug would break.
